# Security

## What Rokh promises, and what it does not

Rokh seals the vessel a carrier holds: opened without Rokh it shows no name,
no address and no count. It seals every record to the readers of its
address, and it judges every event's authority in that event's own causal
past. It does not hide the size of a vessel, the time it changed, or that it
is a Rokh vessel at all. It cannot protect a ledger on a host that is already
compromised, and it cannot recover a passphrase that is lost. See
section 8 of [the contract of version 1](../docs/contracts/v1.md) for what
cannot be proven or promised.

## Reporting

If you find a way to read what a key was not given, to write what a key was
not granted, to make an event's verdict change after it was judged, or to
open a vessel without its passphrase, please report it privately through
this repository's private vulnerability reporting on GitHub (Security tab,
"Report a vulnerability"). Do not open a public issue for it, and do not
describe it in a mission, a question or a study until it is repaired.

Say what you did, on which version (`rokh version`), and what you observed.
You will get an answer from the owner; there is no bounty and no promised
deadline, only an honest reply.

## Supported versions

Only the latest tagged version receives fixes.
